# Introduction & Question

The British Columbia (BC) socioeconomic index (SEI) is a data set provided by 
BC Stats which uses measures of income, health, education, and community
cohesion to develop a well-being indicator by municipality or community health 
service area [@bcstats2026sei]. The data is accessed through proprietary code
provided by BC Stats which allows researchers to get provincial data. The SEI
index is a data set provided by the government that allow for meaningful
sociological analysis, giving a holistic measure of social well-being across
municipal regions in the province. As such, I plan to use this data set to
undertake a exploratory descriptive analysis of SEI scores across 
municipal regions. To achieve this, I will ask the following research
question:

RQ: How does socioeconomic index (SEI) differ across different municipal regions 
in BC?

This question will allow me to use a tibble from the Tidyverse to view the
SEI index in a table and various graph formats [@Tidyverse].

Select "2" to get Census Subdivision Data. This type of data aggregates regions 
into municipalities, not health regions, which are usually smaller [@bcstats2026sei].

# Simulate

```{r}
set.seed(1738)

simulated_ses_data <- tibble(
  City = c("Victoria", "Oak Bay", "Vancouver", "Burnaby"),
  Economics = sample(1:100, size = 4),
  Education = sample(1:100, size = 4),
  Health = sample(1:100, size = 4),
  Community = sample(1:100, size = 4),
  SEI = rowMeans(data.frame(Economics, Education, Health, Community))
)

simulated_ses_data
```

The code chunk above runs a simulation that randomly assigns values from 1-100
in domains of income (economics), education level, population health variables, 
and community cohesion variables. The socioeconomic index (SEI) takes scores 
on each of these domains to calculate an overall index and to show scores on
each domain [@bcdata].

```{r}
simulated_ses_data |>
  tt()
```

The code above uses Tinytable to print a cleaner table of the simulated data 
[@Tinytable].
